messages.subject_clean: [geomorph-r-package] Are pairwise p-values from advanced.procD.lm adjusted?
messages.body_plain:
No, the pairwise comparisons are not pre-adjusted by any experiment-wise error rate. They represent the actual observed probability of the pairwise comparison relative to the distribution of outcomes from permutation. Any such adjustment is a decision left for the individual user, and should be performed in a post-hoc manner following the actual assessment of significance.

Thus, if one wishes to compare the observed pairwise significance to the nominal alpha  = 0.05, or the Bonferroni-adjusted value (alpha/k-comparisons), or the Dunn-Sidak value, or sequential Bonferroni, or otherwise, they may do so accordingly. Note that this post-hoc approach is, in fact, consistent with proper statistical theory (though not always practice in some circles).  Statistically speaking, such adjustments should always be considered an adjustment of the comparison alpha, not an adjustment to the observed probability value.

messages.subject_clean: Problems turning digitsurface result into an array in order to perform GPA
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am a researcher attempting to compare thyroid cartilage (in PLY format) from two different rodent specimens. I am a novice to R, so I have been attempting to learn as much as I can from the geomorph manual and the forum here.

I have been able to define homologous landmarks, create a template, and perform the digitsurface function all without issue. My problem comes when I try to turn the digitsurface results into an array (which I believe is needed to perform the gpagen function.

After viewing the coordinates of the LMM2 array, the data appears scattered and no longer resembles the thyroid shape. Can anyone give me a clue to why this is happening, if I am completing the array function incorrectly, or if there is another way to perform the GPA without having to turn the data into an array?

If anyone can give me some more information on what I am doing wrong or any other way to perform the GPA while still maintaining the thyroid shape in order to normalize the data and compare with other thyroid shapes, please share with me. I have attached images detailing the steps I have taken and below is the code I have used:

LMM2<-read.ply("LMM2-Thyroid.ply") #read LMM2 ply file (3D surface of thyroid cartilage for specimen 1)

LMM3<-read.ply("LMM3_Thyroid.ply") #read LMM3 ply file (3D surface of thyroid cartilage for specimen 2)

a<-digit.fixed(LMM3,40) #manually place landmarks on the 3D surface in a line along the contour you want to capture

LMdata<-digitsurface(LMM2, a, ptsize=1, center=TRUE) #digitize surface of LMM2 using the fixed landmark data specified on LMM3

LMM2LM<-readland.nts("LMM2.nts") #reads the digitized surface result

X<-LMM2LM[,,] #turn data into an array

LMM2Array<-arrayspecs(X,140,3) #specifications of array

plotAllSpecimens(LMM2Array)

Thank you for any information you can provide.

messages.body_plain:
Dear Heather,

As Dean said, there's no reason you should be taking those additional steps, and as such you are making it more difficult for yourself.

But also there's a simple solution to why you are having trouble: you are using the wrong function

You are reading in a single .nts file at line

LMM2LM<-readland.nts("LMM2.nts") #reads the digitized surface result

using the wrong function. The function you need is readmulti.nts. The two functions are different - they read different types of NTS files; the former a single NTS file containing coordinate data for multiple specimens, and the latter for single NTS files each containing coordinate data for a single specimen.  (I have updated the help pages for these two functions in geomorph 3.0.4 coming very soon to CRAN to hopefully make this extra clear).

Anyway, if you do:
LMM2LM<-readmulti.nts("LMM2.nts") #reads the digitized surface result
You'll end up with LMM2LM being a 3D array, containing a single specimen

Emma

messages.subject: geomorph 3.0.4 now available
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

Just a quick announcement to let you know that geomorph version 3.0.4 is now available on CRAN. The list of new features is below, and includes:

o An option to use types I, II, or III sums of squares and cross-products for ANOVA analyses (e.g., procD.lm, procD.pgls)

    o PGLS option for advanced.procD.lm

    o An option to choose between SS, F-values, or Cohen's f-squared to calculate effect sizes for ANOVA analyses (where applicable: see help files).

    o Effect sizes are now centered on mean values from distributions of random statistics.  Statistics are also log-transformed in certain cases to normalize distributions.

    o An option to use only an intercept as a model for procD.lm and procD.pgls, with limited output.

    o An option to use permutation tests when comparing net evolutionary rates for compare.evol.rates

    o New function interlmkdist to calculate linear distances between landmarks

Other changes are listed in the News file.

As always, the most up to date version of geomorph may be found on Github: https://github.com/geomorphR/geomorph

Best,

Dean, Mike, Emma, and Antigoni (the geomorph team)

messages.subject: Re: gpagen with 2D dataset
messages.body_plain:
Dear Avi,

So now that you've read in your coordinate data into the coords function, you need to rearrange the data into an array format for use with geomorph functions. See my user guide <https://github.com/geomorphR/geomorph/raw/gh-pages/geomorph%20user%20guide/Quick_Guide_to_Geomorph-3.0.pdf> for details, but simply:

Y <- arrayspecs(coords, k=2, p = ncol(coords)/2)

This function needs to know how many dimensions the data are (here 2 you said) and the number of landmarks (which is the number of columns in coords divided by 2).

Now you can perform the GPA using gpagen on Y.

To specify which semilandmarks are slding semilandmarks on a curve, you need a matrix that specifies for each slider the 2 landmarks it slides between. Again, see my user guide for this. i.e. if you have a sliding semilandmarks 5 and it slides between 8 and 12, then:

curves <- matrix(c(8,5,12), ncol=3)

Finally two ways to know if the data are already superimposed
1) Look at the data with plotAllSpecimens(Y). If they are all nicely aligned configurations the data probably are superimposed
2) Look at the numbers on the axes and in the Y array - are they decimal, below 1, and centred around 0? if so they probably are superimposed.

Emma

The way I would do this is to manually place lots of fixed landmarks along the curve you are looking at, and then use the digit.curves function to take those landmark coordinates (as a matrix) and resample them as equidistant semilandmarks. Emma

As a tip when something like this happens again, at least in R Studio, if one types, e.g., symData$, a list should appear, which gets smaller as one keeps typing.  Selecting an object from the list guarantees a match to the objects that are available.  R does not return an error when one requests an object that does not exist; it returns NULL.  Therefore, I often start typing the object after “$” that I want and then select it, having R fill in the remainder of characters, so that I make sure not to type the wrong word.

Cheers
Mike

messages.body_plain:
Hello Dr. Adams,

I have used the intercept function for f2 for quite some time when using advanced.procD.lm, particularly with single-factor models. I have, however, found something unusual since the 3.04 update.

a simple example I've been working involves a bivalve species sampled from four localities:

gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(gpa, locality = classifier$Locality)

procD.lm(coords ~ locality, iter = 999, data = gdf)

# Resulting p-value of 0.001, now I want to do pairwise comparisons

advanced.procD.lm(coords ~ locality, ~ 1, groups = ~ locality, iter = 999, data = gdf)

# This has worked until the 3.0.4 update, now I get this error:

Error in array(x, c(length(x), 1L), if (!is.null(names(x))) list(names(x),  :
  'data' must be of a vector type, was 'NULL'

# any model that doesn't use the intercept (~1) does not cause this issue

I can't seem to find an explanation in the package help file, so any assistance would be much appreciated.

Cheers,
Broc

Hi guys,

Thank you, Mike, Miriam, and Emma, for the fast response! I'm not used to that and I appreciate it.

I'm still getting used to the plotting in R though. When I use the plot() function with no extra arguments I get this error that makes reference to the xlabel, which I believe means that there are many xlabels to choose from and I have to specify more:

  formal argument "xlab" matched by multiple actual arguments

But if I use this line of code like Miriam said I do get the dispersion graph of the 3D LM configurations:
>  x11(); plotAllSpecimens(FA$asymm.shape)

Now I wanted to plot the "bilat.symmetry$FA.component" fluctuating asymmetry component as a vector from the consensus configuration. I used this code and get the 3D LM configuration, but I do not know how to command the function to make the vectors representing the LM deviations from the mean:

>  x11(); plotAllSpecimens(FA$FA.component, mean=T,links=NULL)

How can I indicate the plotAllSpecimens() function to represent the fluctuating asymmetry component as vectors from the mean in R in this situation?

All help is appreciated, thank you all!

Best wishes,

Javier
